notes: freq_band_low_hz/freq_band_high_hz are derived from reference-recording acoustics and should transfer across deployments. onset_threshold_factor reflects the source recordings' own background noise, not any particular property's field SNR -- treat it as a starting point and re-validate against real pulled TDOA attempts before trusting it long-term. See tools/README.md.

Bush Stone Curlew.notes: Derived 2026-07-25 from 152 calls across 5 unique Xeno-canto samples (7 downloaded, 2 exact-duplicate files dropped: XC589420, XC597375) via tools/derive_species_bands.py's automated energy-envelope call segmentation + derive_band (5-95th percentile cumulative spectral energy, 150Hz margin). Band = 10th percentile low_hz to 90th percentile high_hz across all scored calls (not a single median) to cover the real spread of call content rather than collapsing to one point -- see tools/derive_species_bands.py's module docstring for why a discrete-cluster approach was tried first and rejected. onset_threshold_factor corrected 2026-07-25 (later same day) from 8.0 to 6.0 -- 8.0 was wrongly assumed to be the live '__default__' fallback value; the actual live default is 6.0 (Jon set it directly, picked as the highest value among the species actually tuned at the time, no other considered rationale), so the species-specific row was accidentally more conservative than just leaving it unconfigured. Zero real detections on this property so far (no arrived/onset_failed rows), so 6.0 (matching the live default) is the right placeholder until real field data exists -- see tools/derive_onset_thresholds.py discussion and project memory on this correction.

Gray Butcherbird.notes: Reprocessed 2026-07-25 (supersedes the 2026-07-13 hand-derived value) using tools/derive_species_bands.py: 139 calls scored across 7 unique Xeno-canto samples (8 downloaded, XC640428 dropped as a content-duplicate of XC635936 -- confirmed via duration + fingerprint match, same underlying recording re-listed under a different catalog number, matching the prior manual finding). Band = 10th percentile low_hz to 90th percentile high_hz across all scored calls, wider than the 2026-07-13 tight-cluster value on both edges -- an earlier attempt this session tried splitting calls into discrete high/low clusters and taking a union of cluster medians, but the underlying distribution turned out to be a smooth continuum with no real gap, so a percentile range was used instead (see tools/derive_species_bands.py's aggregate_species() docstring). onset_threshold_factor updated 2026-07-25 (later same day, real-field pass) from 6.0 to 5.54 -- p90 of the peak_envelope/background ratio measured across 744 real tdoa_attempt_nodes rows (arrived + onset_failed) on this property, the best-sampled species by far. p90 (not median) chosen deliberately: only failures whose ratio exceeded this bar flip to passing (~top 10% closest to the old threshold), an intentionally conservative recovery given a false accept silently corrupts a TDOA solve while an onset_failed is loud and harmless -- see project memory on this discussion. This first pass only used the failure side of the distribution (only onset_failed rows logged their ratio at the time); success-side onset_ratio logging (tdoa_attempt_nodes.onset_ratio) was added the same day so a future re-derivation can use arrived rows too.

Laughing Kookaburra.notes: Derived 2026-07-25 from 29 calls across 7 Xeno-canto samples (2 of the 7 files scored zero calls -- too quiet for the segmentation threshold used, not further investigated) via tools/derive_species_bands.py's automated energy-envelope call segmentation + derive_band (5-95th percentile cumulative spectral energy, 150Hz margin). Band = 10th percentile low_hz to 90th percentile high_hz across all scored calls. Lower call count than other species in this batch -- treat this band with somewhat less confidence than the others derived the same day; worth adding more reference recordings if this species proves to be a common trigger source. onset_threshold_factor briefly corrected 2026-07-25 from 8.0 to 6.0 (matching the live '__default__' fallback, which turned out to actually be 6.0 not the assumed factory 8.0) before a real-field pass superseded it same day: 7.24, p90 of the peak_envelope/background ratio across 11 real tdoa_attempt_nodes rows on this property -- these failures mostly predate this species having its own config row, so ran against whatever the effective default was at the time (likely the 8.0 factory default, not the 6.0 override, which explains why p90 sits close to 8.0 rather than below 6.0). n=11 is thin -- treat this value as provisional, low-confidence, and revisit once more real attempts accumulate (success-side onset_ratio logging was added the same day, see Gray Butcherbird's notes for detail on that change).

Noisy Miner.notes: Reprocessed 2026-07-25 (second pass, same day as the initial 6-species batch) using tools/derive_species_bands.py. The initial run used the same call-segmentation --threshold-factor (6.0) as every other species and scored only 26 calls, with 3 of 7 source files scoring zero -- too quiet for that threshold. Rerunning with --threshold-factor 3.0 recovered signal from 2 of those 3 (XC60735, XC60739) but pushed the proposed band even higher (1237-17905Hz), not lower. Per-file inspection found the real cause: XC837694 alone contributed 51 of 93 scored segments at that threshold, with a consistently extreme high edge (median 16667Hz, max 19339Hz) at regular ~0.5-0.7s intervals across the whole ~40s clip -- a pattern consistent with a continuous insect/cicada chorus rather than sparse bird calls, not confirmed by ear. Excluding XC837694 (done ad-hoc for this run, not yet a reusable --exclude-files option in tools/derive_species_bands.py -- see project memory) while keeping --threshold-factor 3.0 gives 724-9369Hz off the remaining 42 calls across 6 files, rounded to 720-9370. Band = 10th percentile low_hz to 90th percentile high_hz, same method as every other species. Note the call-segmentation threshold-factor used to derive this band (3.0) differs from every other species processed this way (6.0) -- that's a tuning parameter of the derivation script only, unrelated to onset_threshold_factor below (which governs real-time onset detection on the hub, not band derivation). onset_threshold_factor updated 2026-07-25 (later same day, real-field pass) from 5.0 (the 2026-07-13 hand-derived value) to 4.57 -- p90 of the peak_envelope/background ratio across 271 real tdoa_attempt_nodes rows on this property, well-sampled. See Gray Butcherbird's notes for the full p90-vs-median rationale (conservative recovery of only the closest near-misses) and the same-day addition of success-side onset_ratio logging.
